article_content: A teacher in China, Lin Xin, faced severe consequences for defying local authorities' orders to evict her parents from their home. She was compelled to divorce her husband and subsequently lost her position at Minhou No4 Middle School, located in Fujian province. Lin Xin was initially instructed to remove her parents from their residence and demolish it earlier in the year. Ignoring what she deemed 'ridiculous' orders from the local government, she ultimately paid the price with her job and family life. Ms. Lin, a teacher at Minhou No4 Middle School, recounted that her initial understanding of the directive was to persuade her parents to vacate their property. However, it soon became clear that the authorities expected her and her husband to personally demolish the home. She stated, 'I find this utterly ridiculous. Had I simply been asked to influence my parents, I would have complied. But being asked to demolish it myself is simply unbelievable. I am a teacher, and I cannot do that. I am supposed to be a role model. My students would condemn me, and I would be unable to teach in the future.' The reason for needing the land remains unclear, but land seizures are among the primary causes of social unrest in China, exposing a troubling aspect of the country's rapid urbanization that has propelled it to become the world's second-largest economy. Ms. Lin disregarded the local Party Committee's request during the summer. Upon returning to school in September, she was shocked to learn from the headmaster that she was suspended and would not be allowed to teach until her parents' home was demolished. Despite not violating any explicit regulations, the decision was made based on a document signed by local officials. To shield her husband, also a teacher at the same school, from the controversy, Ms. Lin made the difficult choice to divorce him last month. They now live separately and share childcare responsibilities for their young child. The previous month, the story of Xu Haifeng came to light. Three years prior, her home was destroyed, prompting her to travel to Beijing to file a complaint against the city and county governments responsible for the demolition. Land disputes are a leading cause of the numerous protests that occur across China annually. Since then, Xu Haifeng reported that her family members have been kidnapped at least 18 times, typically being blindfolded and taken to a hotel-turned-illegal jail in Wuxi, where they were confined for weeks in small, windowless rooms. Xu's story is appalling, even in a nation accustomed to accounts of arbitrary and sometimes violent land expropriations. It highlights how the financial strain on China's local governments extends beyond the banking sector and affects the lives of ordinary citizens, as desperate authorities resort to extreme measures to secure funds. 'Our Wuxi is deeply in debt,' Xu stated. 'The city now relies on exploiting residents' financial resources and seizing their land for survival.' She claims that her 74-year-old mother has been abducted nearly a dozen times and illegally detained for almost a year in an effort to silence the family's demands for fair compensation. Amnesty International reported last year that land grabs have increased as the economy slows and local governments seek funds to alleviate debt, although some experts dispute this finding. Official data on land grabs is unavailable. Reports indicate that local authorities across China derive between 20 and 90 percent of their income from selling expropriated land. Land disputes are a major cause of the tens of thousands of protests across China each year. Most of these protests go unreported, but some, such as the revolt in Wukan in 2011, have gained significant attention and prompted promises of action from Beijing. Last month, a four-year-old girl was killed by a bulldozer while it was demolishing her home during a land grab in Fujian province, according to local media reports.
translated_content: Wata malama a ƙasar Sin, Lin Xin, ta fuskanci matsaloli masu tsanani saboda ƙin bin umarnin mahukuntan yankin na korar iyayenta daga gidansu. An tilasta mata ta saki mijinta kuma daga bisani ta rasa matsayinta a Makarantar Sakandare ta Minhou No4, dake lardin Fujian. An fara umartar Lin Xin da ta cire iyayenta daga gidansu ta rushe shi a farkon shekarar. Ta yi watsi da abin da ta ɗauka a matsayin umarni 'abin dariya' daga gwamnatin yankin, daga ƙarshe ta biya farashin da aikinta da rayuwar iyalinta. Ms. Lin, malama a Makarantar Sakandare ta Minhou No4, ta bayyana cewa fahimtarta ta farko game da umarnin ita ce ta shawo kan iyayenta su bar gidansu. Duk da haka, ba da jimawa ba ya bayyana a sarari cewa mahukuntan suna tsammanin ita da mijinta su rushe gidan da kansu. Ta bayyana cewa, 'Na ga wannan abin dariya ne. Da an kawai ce na yi wa iyayena tasiri, da na yarda. Amma a ce an tambaye ni in rushe shi da kaina ba abu ne mai yiwuwa ba. Ni malama ce, kuma ba zan iya yin hakan ba. Ya kamata in zama abin koyi. Ɗaliban na za su zarge ni, kuma ba zan iya koyarwa a nan gaba ba.' Dalilin buƙatar filin bai bayyana ba, amma kwace filaye na daga cikin manyan abubuwan da ke haifar da rashin zaman lafiya a ƙasar Sin, wanda ke fallasa wani ɓangare mai wahala na bunƙasuwar birane da ta sa ta zama tattalin arziƙi na biyu mafi girma a duniya. Ms. Lin ta yi watsi da buƙatar Kwamitin Jam'iyyar na yankin a lokacin rani. Da ta koma makaranta a watan Satumba, ta kaɗu da jin daga shugaban makarantar cewa an dakatar da ita kuma ba za a ba ta damar koyarwa ba sai an rushe gidan iyayenta. Duk da cewa ba ta karya wata doka ba, an yanke shawarar ne bisa wata takarda da jami'an yankin suka sanya wa hannu. Domin kare mijinta, wanda shi ma malami ne a makaranta ɗaya, daga takaddama, Ms. Lin ta yanke shawara mai wuya na sake shi a watan da ya gabata. A yanzu suna zaune dabam kuma suna raba nauyin kula da yaron su. A watan da ya gabata, labarin Xu Haifeng ya fito fili. Shekaru uku da suka gabata, an lalata gidanta, wanda ya sa ta yi tafiya zuwa Beijing don shigar da ƙara a kan gwamnatocin birni da gunduma da ke da alhakin rushewar. Rigingimun filaye na daga cikin manyan abubuwan da ke haifar da dimbin zanga-zangar da ke faruwa a faɗin ƙasar Sin duk shekara. Tun daga nan, Xu Haifeng ta ruwaito cewa an sace 'yan uwa aƙalla sau 18, yawanci ana ɗaure su ido a kai su wani otal da aka mayar da gidan yari ba bisa ƙa'ida ba a Wuxi, inda aka tsare su na makwanni a cikin ƙananan ɗakuna marasa tagogi. Labarin Xu abin ban tsoro ne, har ma a cikin al'ummar da ta saba da labarun kwace filaye ba bisa ƙa'ida ba da kuma tashin hankali. Ya nuna yadda matsin kuɗi a kananan hukumomin ƙasar Sin ya wuce fannin banki kuma ya shafi rayuwar talakawa, yayin da hukumomi masu neman tsira ke neman hanyoyin da za su samu kuɗi. 'Wuxi ɗinmu na cikin bashi mai yawa,' in ji Xu. 'Birnin a yanzu ya dogara ne da amfani da dukiyar mazauna da kwace filayensu don tsira.' Ta yi ikirarin cewa an sace mahaifiyarta mai shekaru 74 kusan sau goma sha biyu kuma an tsare ta ba bisa ƙa'ida ba kusan shekara guda a wani yunƙuri na dakatar da buƙatar iyalan na neman diyya mai kyau. Ƙungiyar Amnesty International ta ruwaito a bara cewa kwace filaye ya ƙaru yayin da tattalin arziƙi ke raguwa kuma kananan hukumomi ke neman kuɗi don rage basussuka, kodayake wasu masana sun musanta wannan gano. Babu bayanan hukuma game da kwace filaye. Rahotanni sun nuna cewa kananan hukumomi a faɗin ƙasar Sin suna samun tsakanin kashi 20 zuwa 90 na kuɗaɗen shigarsu daga sayar da filayen da aka kwace. Rigingimun filaye na daga cikin manyan abubuwan da ke haifar da dimbin zanga-zangar da ke faruwa a faɗin ƙasar Sin duk shekara. Yawancin waɗannan zanga-zangar ba a ba da rahotonsu ba, amma wasu, kamar tawayen da aka yi a Wukan a 2011, sun samu kulawa sosai kuma sun haifar da alkawuran ɗaukar mataki daga Beijing. A watan da ya gabata, wata yarinya 'yar shekara huɗu ta mutu sakamakon wani bulldozer yayin da yake rushe gidanta a lokacin kwace filaye a lardin Fujian, a cewar rahotannin kafofin watsa labarai na yankin.

article_content: In Alirajpur, Madhya Pradesh, a region marked by a high tribal population, life is challenging. Seventeen-year-old Anil Bedia, like many others, faces daily struggles. Despite frequent power outages that force him to adjust his study space for optimal light, Anil holds a strong ambition: to become a doctor. He dreams of providing much-needed orthopaedic services to his community, which lacks basic healthcare. Alirajpur, carved out of Jhabua district in 2008, is now recognized as one of the poorest districts in the state, according to the NITI Aayog. Its low literacy rate of 37% stands in stark contrast to the state average of 70.06%. Shankar Tadwal, a social worker, points out that many adults migrate to Gujarat for work, leaving behind a district populated mainly by the elderly and young children. This mass migration is driven by poor agricultural returns, with many families owning very small plots of land, averaging around 0.25 hectare. Child labor is a serious concern, with children frequently observed traveling to Gujarat. As the election approaches, there are fears of low voter turnout due to the high number of migrant workers. The local administration claims they are making efforts to encourage these workers to return and vote. Development schemes aimed at alleviating poverty face significant hurdles. Illiteracy, biometric authentication failures, and errors in documentation prevent many tribal people from accessing these benefits. Tadwal argues that the government needs to proactively reach out to these communities to ensure they can participate in these programs. Collector Bedekar acknowledges the difficulty but emphasizes the importance of these efforts. In the political landscape, the Congress party initially held both Assembly seats, but the BJP won a subsequent by-election in Jobat in 2021. Key issues remain agricultural support and employment opportunities, with the Congress MLA highlighting the lack of basic amenities in the area.
translated_content: A Alirajpur, jihar Madhya Pradesh, wani yanki da ke da yawan kabilu, rayuwa na da ƙalubale. Matashi Anil Bedia mai shekaru goma sha bakwai, kamar sauran mutane da yawa, yana fuskantar matsaloli na yau da kullum. Duk da yawan katsewar wutar lantarki da ke tilasta masa daidaita wurin karatunsa don samun haske mai kyau, Anil yana da babban buri: ya zama likita. Yana mafarkin samar da ayyukan kula da kashi da ake buƙata ga al'ummarsa, wadda ba ta da kayan aikin kiwon lafiya na asali. Alirajpur, wadda aka sassaka daga gundumar Jhabua a shekarar 2008, an san ta a matsayin ɗaya daga cikin gundumomi mafi talauci a jihar, a cewar NITI Aayog. Ƙarancin karatunta na kashi 37% ya yi matuƙar bambanta da matsakaicin jihar na kashi 70.06%. Shankar Tadwal, wani ma'aikacin jin kai, ya nuna cewa manya da yawa suna hijira zuwa Gujarat don aiki, suna barin gundumar da ta kunshi tsofaffi da ƙananan yara. Wannan hijira mai yawa ta samo asali ne daga rashin samun kuɗin shiga daga aikin noma, inda iyalai da yawa ke da ƙananan filaye, waɗanda ke da matsakaicin kadada 0.25. Aikin ƙananan yara babban abin damuwa ne, inda ake yawan ganin yara suna tafiya zuwa Gujarat. Yayin da zaɓen ke gabatowa, ana fargabar ƙarancin masu kaɗa ƙuri'a saboda yawan ma'aikatan da suka yi hijira. Hukumar yankin ta yi ikirarin cewa suna ƙoƙarin ƙarfafa waɗannan ma'aikata su koma gida su kaɗa ƙuri'a. Shirye-shiryen raya ƙasa da nufin rage talauci na fuskantar manyan matsaloli. Rashin ilimi, gaza warar tantance bayanan halittu, da kurakurai a cikin takardu suna hana mutanen kabilu da yawa samun waɗannan fa'idodin. Tadwal ya bayar da hujjar cewa gwamnati na buƙatar ta tuntubi waɗannan al'ummomi don tabbatar da cewa za su iya shiga cikin waɗannan shirye-shiryen. Collector Bedekar ya amince da wahalar amma ya jaddada muhimmancin waɗannan ƙoƙarin. A siyasance, jam'iyyar Congress ta fara riƙe kujerun majalisa guda biyu, amma jam'iyyar BJP ta lashe zaɓen fidda gwani a Jobat a shekarar 2021. Muhimman batutuwa sun kasance tallafin aikin noma da damar aikin yi, inda ɗan majalisar Congress ya jaddada rashin kayayyakin more rayuwa a yankin.

article_content: On February 14, when Netflix aired Season 2 of 'House of Cards,' my book, 'The Last Great Senate,' appeared on Vice President Francis Underwood's desk in Episode 2. It was unexpected and somewhat incongruous. I can't think of anyone less likely to read, or be inspired by, my history of the great Senate than the scheming Underwood, except perhaps Sen. Mitch McConnell. McConnell, seeking his sixth term, defeated Matt Bevin in the Republican primary on May 20. He has improved the Republican's chances of capturing the Senate by working to defeat other tea party nominees. As McConnell campaigns against Alison Grimes, it's a good time to assess the damage he has inflicted on the Senate over the past 5.5 years. Mitch McConnell didn't create the hyper-partisan Senate, which has been declining since the mid-1990s. However, through a calculated strategy, McConnell drove the Senate to a new low. When Barack Obama took office in January 2009, America was nearing a second Great Depression. We lost many jobs monthly. Despite the crisis, Obama faced partisan opposition. On the stimulus, healthcare, and financial regulation, McConnell worked to keep Republicans united in opposition. By objective measures, the Senate has become dysfunctional. It has failed as 'the nation's mediator.' Debate, compromise, and the national interest have been sacrificed for partisan advantage. This strategy is cynical because McConnell knows what the Senate should be. Unlike Trent Lott, who disliked the Senate, and Bill Frist, who didn't understand it, McConnell grew up in the 'great Senate' of the 1960s and 1970s. He has invoked Mike Mansfield's name, noting Mansfield built a Senate based on 'mutual trust and respect.' Mansfield treated everyone with respect and understood the need to work with the president, regardless of party. He was admired for his knowledge and believed senators should prioritize collective action. In Mansfield's Senate, the national interest and the institution were paramount. No Senate leader could differ more from Mansfield than McConnell. He has shown contempt for the President, denounced opponents, and opposed deals to streamline nominations. He prioritized denying Obama re-election over the country's interests. He has deadlocked the Senate for partisan gain. Republicans attack Harry Reid in response, but Reid is trying to enact the President's program, while McConnell obstructs. The divide in the Senate is larger than in the 1960s-1980s, making strong leadership crucial. McConnell has worsened partisan differences. From 2013, senators wanted the Senate to return to 'regular order': legislating through committees, considering amendments, debating, and compromising. The Senate showed signs of progress on issues like immigration and the budget, as Republicans worked together. They had to work around McConnell. Leaders set the tone. The Senate would be different under leaders like Lamar Alexander, Rob Portman, Susan Collins, or Bob Corker. In 2012, McConnell anticipated becoming Majority Leader, but Obama was re-elected, rejecting obstruction. Now, he's betting on low poll numbers and turnout, presenting himself as a restorer of the Senate. McConnell shares 'the audacity of hope' with Obama. He hopes people forget the past 5.5 years. Kentucky voters will decide his fate, but the verdict on his damage to the Senate is already in.
translated_content: A ranar 14 ga Fabrairu, lokacin da Netflix ya nuna Season na 2 na 'House of Cards,' littafina, 'The Last Great Senate,' ya bayyana a kan teburin Mataimakin Shugaban Kasa Francis Underwood a Episode na 2. Ba zato ba tsammani ne kuma ya ɗan yi kama da ban mamaki. Ba zan iya tunanin wani wanda ba zai karanta ba, ko kuma ya samu kwarin gwiwa daga tarihin majalisata mai girma kamar Underwood mai shiririta, sai dai watakila Sanata Mitch McConnell. McConnell, yana neman wa'adi na shida, ya doke Matt Bevin a zaɓen fidda gwani na Republican a ranar 20 ga Mayu. Ya inganta damar Republican na kama Majalisar Dattawa ta hanyar aiki don kayar da sauran 'yan takarar jam'iyyar Tea Party. Yayin da McConnell ke yaƙin neman zaɓe da Alison Grimes, lokaci ya yi da za a kimanta barnar da ya yi wa Majalisar Dattawa a cikin shekaru 5.5 da suka gabata. Mitch McConnell bai ƙirƙiro majalisar dattawa mai tsattsauran ra'ayi ba, wacce ke ta tabarbarewa tun tsakiyar shekarun 1990. Koyaya, ta hanyar dabara mai lissafi, McConnell ya kai Majalisar Dattawa ga sabon matsayi mai ƙasƙanci. Lokacin da Barack Obama ya hau mulki a watan Janairu 2009, Amurka na gab da shiga cikin Babban Bacin Rai na biyu. Mun rasa ayyuka da yawa kowane wata. Duk da rikicin, Obama ya fuskanci adawar jam'iyya. Kan batun ƙara kuzari, kiwon lafiya, da kuma tsarin kuɗi, McConnell ya yi aiki don ci gaba da haɗa kan 'yan Republican a cikin adawa. Ta hanyar ma'auni na gaskiya, Majalisar Dattawa ta zama mai matsala. Ta gaza a matsayin 'mai shiga tsakani na ƙasa.' Muhawara, sulhu, da kuma bukatun ƙasa an sadaukar da su don amfanin jam'iyya. Wannan dabarar ta zama abin zargi saboda McConnell ya san yadda Majalisar Dattawa ya kamata ta kasance. Ba kamar Trent Lott ba, wanda ba ya son Majalisar Dattawa, da Bill Frist, wanda bai gane ta ba, McConnell ya girma a cikin 'Majalisar Dattawa mai girma' na shekarun 1960 da 1970. Ya ambaci sunan Mike Mansfield, yana mai lura da cewa Mansfield ya gina Majalisar Dattawa bisa 'amana da girmamawa juna.' Mansfield ya mutunta kowa kuma ya fahimci buƙatar yin aiki tare da shugaban ƙasa, ba tare da la'akari da jam'iyya ba. An yaba masa saboda iliminsa kuma ya yi imanin ya kamata Sanatoci su ba da fifiko ga haɗin gwiwa. A Majalisar Dattawa ta Mansfield, bukatun ƙasa da cibiyar sun kasance mafi muhimmanci. Babu wani shugaban Majalisar Dattawa da zai bambanta da Mansfield kamar McConnell. Ya nuna raini ga Shugaban ƙasa, ya soki abokan hamayyarsa, kuma ya ƙi amincewa da yarjejeniyoyin da za su sauƙaƙa naɗin mukamai. Ya ba da fifiko wajen hana Obama sake zaɓe a kan bukatun ƙasar. Ya tsayar da Majalisar Dattawa don samun riba ta jam'iyya. 'Yan Republican sun kai hari kan Harry Reid a matsayin martani, amma Reid yana ƙoƙarin aiwatar da shirin Shugaban ƙasar, yayin da McConnell ke kawo cikas. Rarrabuwar kawuna a Majalisar Dattawa ta fi girma fiye da a cikin shekarun 1960-1980, wanda ya sa ƙarfin shugabanci ya zama dole. McConnell ya ƙara tsananta bambance-bambancen jam'iyya. Tun daga shekarar 2013, Sanatoci sun so Majalisar Dattawa ta koma kan 'tsari na yau da kullum': yin doka ta hanyar kwamitoci, la'akari da gyare-gyare, muhawara, da sulhu. Majalisar Dattawa ta nuna alamun ci gaba kan batutuwa kamar shige da fice da kasafin kuɗi, yayin da 'yan Republican suka yi aiki tare. Dole ne su yi aiki a kusa da McConnell. Shugabanni sun kafa yanayin. Majalisar Dattawa za ta bambanta a ƙarƙashin shugabannin kamar Lamar Alexander, Rob Portman, Susan Collins, ko Bob Corker. A cikin 2012, McConnell ya yi tsammanin zama Shugaban Masu Rinjaye, amma an sake zaɓen Obama, inda aka ƙi amincewa da kawo cikas. Yanzu, yana yin fare akan ƙananan ƙididdiga da fitowar jama'a, yana gabatar da kansa a matsayin mai dawo da Majalisar Dattawa. McConnell ya raba 'gaba gaɗin bege' tare da Obama. Yana fatan mutane za su manta da shekaru 5.5 da suka gabata. Masu jefa ƙuri'a na Kentucky za su yanke hukuncin makomarsa, amma an riga an yanke hukuncin barnar da ya yi wa Majalisar Dattawa.

article_content: Louis van Gaal has stated that the recent contract extension of Manchester United defender Tyler Blackett demonstrates the club's ongoing belief in its academy system. The 20-year-old signed a new contract with the club on Thursday, committing him until 2017, with the option of an additional year. Blackett, who is capable of playing in central defence or at left back, has also received a substantial increase in his weekly wage, rising from £2,000 to £20,000. Manchester United defender Tyler Blackett signed a new £20,000-a-week deal at the club on Thursday. Blackett signed the contract, securing his place at the club until 2017. The highly-rated youngster is the last of three academy players to sign a contract extension, following Jesse Lingard and Patrick McNair. Van Gaal has highlighted the new contracts of these three players as part of the club's strategy to integrate more academy graduates into the Manchester United first team. 'Indeed, it is the club's strategy. Upon my arrival, I was informed that they aimed to incorporate more youth academy players into the first team,' he stated on Friday during the club's press conference before their weekend match at home against Sunderland. 'Furthermore, the Premier League rule requiring a certain number of players within your squad to have come through your own system is also significant.' Blackett joins fellow young defender Patrick McNair in signing a new contract extension at the club. Jesse Lingard has also signed a new deal, which Van Gaal believes showcases the value of their academy. 'I am pleased that we can sign players from our youth academy, and our players are highly sought after, as evidenced by the numerous youngsters we have out on loan. This allows us to carefully select clubs where players can gain regular playing time, as we have seen with Reece James, Michael or Will Keane – this is also part of our strategy.' 'I have faith in players who have been developed within our own youth academy; perhaps that is why I am in this position.' Blackett has made 10 appearances this season, his last appearance being on January 11 when United lost 1-0 to Southampton at Old Trafford. Blackett has made 10 appearances for United this season, with his most recent outing against Southampton.

'Ina farin ciki da za mu iya ɗaukar 'yan wasa daga makarantarmu ta koyon ƙwallon ƙafa, kuma 'yan wasanmu suna da matuƙar buƙata, kamar yadda yawancin matasa da muke da su a matsayin aro suka nuna. Wannan yana ba mu damar zaɓar ƙungiyoyi a hankali inda 'yan wasa za su iya samun damar buga wasa akai-akai, kamar yadda muka gani tare da Reece James, Michael ko Will Keane - wannan ma wani ɓangare ne na dabarunmu.' 'Ina da imani ga 'yan wasan da aka bunƙasa a cikin makarantarmu ta koyon ƙwallon ƙafa; watakila shi ya sa nake cikin wannan matsayi.' Blackett ya buga wasanni 10 a wannan kakar, wasansa na ƙarshe ya kasance a ranar 11 ga Janairu lokacin da United ta sha kashi da ci 1-0 a hannun Southampton a Old Trafford. article_content: A mother, known as 'Vodka Mom' after passing out drunk and rolling onto her three-day-old son, suffocating him, died by suicide after weeks of condemnation. Toni Annette Medrano, 29, was heavily criticized after Nancy Grace condemned her carelessness on her cable television show last month. She died from self-inflicted burns after using a flammable liquid in the backyard of a home in St. Paul Park, Minnesota, last Monday. The exact cause of death is under investigation. She had been charged with manslaughter in the death of her newborn son, Adrian, whom she allegedly rolled onto while sleeping on the couch in her Cottage Grove home in November 2011. She reportedly drank a fifth of vodka before falling asleep on the couch with the baby between her and the back cushions. Throughout the night, she woke to feed Adrian and got formula around 3 a.m. She then drifted in and out of sleep. Her other children were preparing for school, according to Pioneer Press. At 10:30 a.m., she found Adrian cold and purple and alerted her husband, Jason. Mr. Medrano had warned her about the risk of suffocating the infant if she slept with him on the couch, according to the St. Paul Star Tribune. Nancy Grace described the events, stating, 'Did mommy booze it up and kill her baby? The mother spent the weekend drinking. She's waking up so drunk off a fifth of vodka she doesn't even know her baby is lying there dead beside her. This woman laid on top of this baby for hours. He had been dead for hours. Isn't it true she stated she had been drinking the entire time and had other children in the home? In fact, the other children wondered about the baby and didn't realize he was dead? There was a long period of time that her baby could have been saved.' When she found Adrian unresponsive, they called 911 and tried to revive him. He was pronounced dead on arrival at Woodwinds Hospital in Woodbury. The official cause of death was 'asphyxia due to being laid upon while sleeping with an adult,' according to the Ramsey County Medical Examiner's office. Medrano's blood alcohol content was 0.11. When the story was featured on Nancy Grace, the host condemned Medrano, stating the amount she drank was equal to 17 vodka drinks. 'She's waking up so drunk off a fifth of vodka she doesn't even know her baby is lying there dead beside her,' Grace said. 'There was a long period of time that her baby could have been saved.' A doctor on the show noted the baby had likely been dead for hours when discovered, indicated by his purple color – a sign of blood pooling. Nancy Grace added that Medrano had a history of heavy drinking, with two DWIs in a month. After the show, Medrano faced condemnation on blogs and social media. She faced two counts of second-degree manslaughter, one for 'culpable negligence creating unreasonable risk' and another for 'committing or attempting to commit a violation.' She could have faced up to 10 years in prison if convicted. Washington County Attorney Pete Orput stated after her son's death, 'Irrespective of the ultimate outcome, I hope valuable lessons can be learned from these tragic circumstances.'

article_content: Former Indian footballer and Hamro Sikkim Party president Bhaichung Bhutia on Thursday merged his party with the Sikkim Democratic Front (SDF), led by Pawan Chamling, during an SDF event in Ravangla district, South Sikkim. Bhaichung, formerly the working president of Hamro Sikkim Party, had been the party's public figure since 2018 and unsuccessfully contested the 2019 elections. In September, Bhaichung Bhutia formally announced his decision to join the Sikkim Democratic Front party led by former Chief Minister Pawan Kumar Chamling. Asked why he chose SDF, Bhutia stated, 'Since the departure of allegedly corrupt leaders, SDF has ostensibly cleansed itself of corruption. For four years, SKM accused Chamling of corruption, but they haven't filed any corruption cases against him, seemingly exonerating Chamling. Furthermore, as an opposition party, SDF has been vocal about Sikkim's issues, exemplified by their 'Save Sikkim' campaign. Bhaichung and SDF hope to achieve great success together'. Prior to the previous election, Bhaichung supported the ruling Sikkim Krantikari Morcha and met with current Chief Minister Prem Singh Golay before the 2019 election. Bhutia explained, 'In 2019, we supported Prem Singh Golay's promise of change (Parivartan). We strategically fielded candidates in constituencies where SKM had weaker candidates, aiming for the change SKM advocated. However, over these past four years, the Parivartan has faltered under Golay and SKM, which is now allegedly rife with corrupt leaders and businessmen who previously undermined 25 years of SDF's work'. In 2014, after retiring from football, Bhutia joined the All India Trinamool Congress and unsuccessfully ran for the Indian general election in the Darjeeling constituency. In 2018, after parting ways with All India Trinamool Congress, he founded the Hamro Sikkim Party in Sikkim.

Tsawon shekaru huɗu, SKM ta zargi Chamling da cin hanci da rashawa, amma ba su shigar da wani ƙara na cin hanci da rashawa a kansa ba, wanda hakan ya nuna cewa Chamling ba shi da laifi. Mun tsara 'yan takara a mazabu inda SKM ke da 'yan takara marasa ƙarfi, da nufin samun canjin da SKM ke shawarta. 'A cikin 2014, bayan ya yi ritaya daga ƙwallon ƙafa, Bhutia ya shiga jam'iyyar All India Trinamool Congress kuma bai yi nasara ba a zaɓen gama gari na Indiya a mazabar Darjeeling.' article_content: In 2011, when the family pet cat Woosie disappeared, his owners presumed him dead. Unbeknownst to them, the tomcat had wandered into a Ginsters pasty factory, approximately 30 miles away, where he was being well-cared for. He enjoyed a rich diet of pastries and sandwiches provided by the staff. Woosie’s adventure ended last week when factory workers decided to take him to the local vet. A scan of his microchip revealed that he belonged to Helen and Phillip Johns of Gover, near St Austell, Cornwall. Woosie has now been returned home. Far from appearing neglected after his three-year absence, Woosie seemed to have gained weight. Helen, a 58-year-old mother of three, said, 'He went out one morning, as cats often do, and we never saw him again.' 'Then, nearly three years later, we received a call from the vet saying they had our cat. I looked at our other cat, Lola, and told them they must be mistaken.' 'Then it suddenly registered that they must mean Woosie. I was so shocked. Home sweet home: Mrs. Johns was stunned when Woosie was found alive and well after running away in 2011. 'The vet said he had been living in the Ginsters pasty factory in Callington and that one of the workers had been looking after him.' 'I was gobsmacked. We never expected to see him again, especially after he’d been missing for three years.' 'He’s a heavy cat now—quite large. We think he may have been eating all the pasties and sandwiches up there.' 'He’s probably been given lots of titbits by the staff there.' Workers adopted Woosie, allowing him free access to the offices during the day, feeding him Ginsters products, and renaming him ‘George.’ Staff at the pasty factory, approximately 30 miles away, said he roamed the grounds outside at night and was always there to greet workers in the morning. Since his return, Mrs. Johns said Woosie had settled in, except for the 'odd hiss' at Lola, their other cat, who was just a kitten when he disappeared. Mrs. Johns said, 'He came home on Tuesday evening, came straight into the house, and just stretched out in the chair as if nothing had happened.' 'He’s like Lord Muck. It’s surreal. He’s unfazed by it.' The grandmother-of-one was dumbfounded as to how Woosie had ended up at the pasty factory near Plymouth. She said, 'We have no idea how he ended up there, but cats are curious.' 'We think he may have climbed into the back of a lorry delivering to the Co-Op store and gone unnoticed by the driver.' 'Or he could have jumped into someone’s car who was visiting the area when they opened the door.' 'We just don’t know. It’s just a miracle he’s here after three years.' Mrs. Johns said the vet had advised her not to let Woosie out for a couple of weeks while he adjusted to his surroundings. 'There is a worry that he will just go off again,' she said. 'But we are just glad to have him home.' Ginsters said they were unaware of the incident but were 'delighted' Woosie had been reunited with his owners. A spokesperson said, 'As you would expect from a food manufacturer, we have very strict procedures to ensure that stray animals do not venture into the perimeter of our premises at any time.' 'We have not been made aware of this particular incident; however, we are always pleased to hear of a nice ending to a story and delighted that Woosie has been reunited with its owners.'

article_content: A vibrant green algae bloom, stretching 120 miles in length and 60 miles in width, is so extensive that it is visible from space. The 'remarkable' bloom was captured by a satellite camera orbiting 400 miles above Earth. It is hypothesized that the bloom originated when snow from Antarctica was blown into the ocean. Australian scientists, who identified the bloom in satellite images, attribute the massive growth to a concentration of iron released from the melting snow. The phenomenon is considered potentially the largest such growth in recent memory, triggering a feeding frenzy among marine life. Krill and plankton are consuming the algae, subsequently becoming prey for larger animals like whales, penguins, and seals. According to reports, scientists suggest that Antarctic snow, carrying trace amounts of iron, was carried into the sea by strong summer winds. Dr. Mark Curran, of the Australian Antarctic Division, explained to ABC Radio that 'very tiny amounts of iron act as a nutrient.' He added, 'Algae in this region are typically iron-limited, so a small addition of iron, coupled with favorable conditions, is sufficient to stimulate a bloom.' The algae eventually dies off, and bacteria feed on the decaying material, which ultimately sinks to the ocean floor, unless consumed by predators higher in the food chain. The algae bloom is believed to have started after strong winds pushed snow from Antarctica into the ocean. Tiny amounts of iron act as a nutrient source, enabling the algae to form and flourish. The algae bloom has created a feeding frenzy, attracting penguins, seals, and other marine life. The images were taken by the Modis instrument on NASA's Terra satellite, which is positioned approximately 400 miles above Earth. This particular algae bloom has persisted on the ocean's surface for three weeks and is expected to dissipate soon. The unconsumed portions will break down naturally, without causing any adverse environmental effects. Dr. Jan Leiser described the phenomenon as a 'remarkable natural event' on The Conversation website: 'Iron is the limiting nutrient in that part of the world, so as soon as you have iron, sunlight, and all other conditions are favorable, these algal blooms thrive and reproduce.' Regarding the source of the iron, Dr. Leiser stated: 'We are not entirely certain. One hypothesis is that strong offshore winds carry snow and sediment from the continent into the ocean, where the melting snow releases the nutrient load.'
translated_content: Wani gagarumin toka mai hasken kore, mai tsawon mil 120 da faɗin mil 60, ya yi girma sosai har ana iya ganinsa daga sararin samaniya. Kyamarar tauraron ɗan adam da ke shawagi a mil 400 sama da duniya ta ɗauki wannan toka mai ban sha'awa. An yi hasashen cewa tokar ta samo asali ne lokacin da aka hura dusar ƙanƙara daga Antarctica zuwa cikin teku. Masana kimiyya na Australiya, waɗanda suka gano tokar a hotunan tauraron ɗan adam, sun danganta gagarumin girman ga tarin ƙarfe da aka saki daga dusar ƙanƙarar da ke narkewa. Ana ɗaukar wannan lamarin a matsayin mai yiwuwa mafi girman irin wannan girma a cikin 'yan kwanakin nan, wanda ya haifar da tashin hankali a tsakanin rayuwar teku. Krill da plankton suna cin algae, daga baya kuma suna zama ganima ga manyan dabbobi kamar whale, penguins, da seals. Dangane da rahotanni, masana kimiyya sun nuna cewa dusar ƙanƙara ta Antarctic, ɗauke da ƙananan ƙarfe, iska mai ƙarfi ta rani ta kai ta cikin teku. Dr. Mark Curran, na Sashen Antarctic na Australiya, ya bayyana wa Gidan Rediyon ABC cewa 'ƙananan adadin ƙarfe suna aiki azaman sinadarai masu gina jiki.' Ya kara da cewa, 'Algae a wannan yankin galibi yana da iyaka na ƙarfe, don haka ƙaramin ƙari na ƙarfe, tare da yanayi mai kyau, ya isa ya motsa toka.' Daga ƙarshe algae yana mutuwa, kuma ƙwayoyin cuta suna cin abubuwan da ke lalacewa, wanda daga ƙarshe ya nutse zuwa kasan teku, sai dai idan masu cin zarafi sun cinye shi a sama a cikin sarkar abinci. An yi imanin cewa tokar algae ta fara ne bayan da iska mai ƙarfi ta tura dusar ƙanƙara daga Antarctica zuwa cikin teku. Ƙananan adadin ƙarfe suna aiki azaman tushen sinadarai, suna ba da damar algae su samu kuma su bunƙasa. Tokar algae ta haifar da tashin hankali, tana jan hankalin penguins, seals, da sauran rayuwar teku. Hotunan Modis ne suka ɗauke su a tauraron ɗan adam na NASA Terra, wanda ke da tazarar mil 400 sama da Duniya. Wannan tokar algae ta musamman ta ci gaba da kasancewa a saman teku har tsawon makonni uku kuma ana sa ran za ta watse nan ba da daɗewa ba. Sassan da ba a cinye su ba za su rushe ta halitta, ba tare da haifar da wani mummunan tasiri na muhalli ba. Dr. Jan Leiser ya bayyana lamarin a matsayin 'gagarumin al'amari na halitta' a gidan yanar gizon The Conversation: 'Ƙarfe shine sinadari mai iyaka a wannan ɓangaren duniya, don haka da zarar kuna da ƙarfe, hasken rana, da duk sauran yanayi sun dace, waɗannan toka na algal suna bunƙasa kuma suna hayayyafa.' Game da tushen ƙarfe, Dr. Leiser ya bayyana: 'Ba mu da tabbacin gaske. Ɗaya daga cikin hasashen shine cewa iska mai ƙarfi ta teku tana ɗaukar dusar ƙanƙara da laka daga nahiyar zuwa cikin teku, inda dusar ƙanƙarar da ke narkewa ke sakin kayan abinci mai gina jiki.'

article_content: Emmanuel Frimpong, once a promising midfielder from Arsenal and a former England youth player, has signed with FC Ufa, a team recently promoted to the Russian Premier League. The 22-year-old is looking to revitalize his career after Barnsley released him last season. Starting his journey at Arsenal, Frimpong initially played for England's Under-17 team. He later chose to represent Ghana at the senior level. He was once highly regarded and tipped to become a key player for Arsenal's midfield. Following his release from Barnsley, Frimpong aims to reignite his career with this move abroad. He previously had loan spells with Wolves, where a serious knee injury cut his time short, and later short stints at Fulham and Charlton before permanently joining Barnsley. article_content: British tourists were among the thousands stranded in the French Alps today after heavy snowfalls made roads impassable, resulting in at least one death. The Savoie region in southeast France was the worst affected, with an estimated 15,000 people impacted. A 27-year-old man died when his car fell into a ravine in the Belledonne mountain range. Temporary shelters were set up in sports centers and town halls across 12 towns to assist those forced to abandon their vehicles. Around 15,000 vehicles were stranded in the French Alps due to the heavy snowfalls that rendered roads impassable. Hundreds of British holidaymakers traveling from Channel ports to ski resorts were among those caught in the disruption. France's Interior Minister, Bernard Cazeneuve, advised those considering driving to 'exercise extreme caution' and only travel 'if absolutely necessary'. Edward Moss, traveling from his home in north London to a resort in Switzerland, stated, 'Traffic stopped as we approached the mountains. Cars were skidding, and the situation became extremely dangerous.' 'We checked into a hotel early as the advice was that we shouldn't take any risks,' he added. Hundreds of British holidaymakers traveling from Channel ports to ski resorts were among those caught in the chaos. Temporary shelters have been set up in sports centres and town halls in 12 towns to help those who had to abandon their cars. Traveler Kate Rhodes told Sky News: 'I am on a coach with several tired and hungry people. Everyone is fine, and the kids are subsisting on Haribo sweets.' 'No emergency services are visible, nor is anyone handing out hot drinks and food to weary drivers, many of whom are with small children en route to their holidays, stuck on the road in freezing temperatures.' 'The situation is very frustrating. The biggest problem is that most people's phones have run out of battery, so they are getting anxious about other friends who are also traveling at this time and informing family that they are safe.' A spokesman for France's meteorological center indicated that more snow was expected along with 'significant re-freezing'. The country issued an orange weather alert - one level below the maximum red alert - in 19 departments. Storms with gusts reaching up to 160 kilometers per hour forced the temporary closure of France's port of Calais on the English Channel and the suspension of car ferries to and from Britain. Holidaymakers wake up after spending the night in a civic hall because roads were blocked due to heavy snowfall in Albertville. Tourists eat breakfast after heavy snowfall in the French Alps left approximately 15,000 drivers stranded. article_content: Paris (CNN) -- Yasser Arafat's widow questioned Tuesday the findings of French scientists that the Palestinian leader died of natural causes, contradicting suspicions of radioactive polonium poisoning. The French conclusion, reported by multiple media outlets including Reuters, contrasts with Swiss forensic scientists who suggested last month that samples from Arafat's exhumed body were consistent with polonium-210 exposure, though they stopped short of confirming poisoning. 'I'm convinced something is wrong, and he didn't die naturally,' Suha Arafat stated at a Paris news conference. She is requesting the Swiss findings be shared with French authorities investigating her husband's death. She noted the differing specializations of experts in Switzerland and France. 'I don't doubt their expertise, but they possess different skills and medical specializations,' she explained. The French findings are unlikely to dispel rumors that Arafat was poisoned. Arafat died at 75 in a Paris military hospital in November 2004 after a brain hemorrhage and subsequent coma. Prior to his death, Palestinian officials reported Arafat had a blood disorder, excluding leukemia, and digestive issues. Poisoning rumors circulated at the time but were denied by Palestinian officials. Two weeks after Arafat's death, his nephew noted medical records lacked a cause of death. Nasser al-Kidwa, then the Palestinian observer to the United Nations, said toxicology tests showed 'no known poison,' but didn't rule out poisoning as a possibility. Polonium-210 gained notoriety in 2006 when used to assassinate Alexander Litvinenko, a former KGB agent who defected to Britain in 2000 after whistleblowing on the FSB, the KGB's successor. In his deathbed statement from a London hospital, Litvinenko accused Russian President Vladimir Putin, which the Kremlin vehemently denied. Palestinians, for whom Arafat is a symbol of resistance, are deeply affected by the poisoning suspicion. Arafat initially led the Palestine Liberation Organization, which conducted attacks against Israeli targets. He later led the Palestinian Authority after parts of the West Bank and Gaza were returned to Palestinian control. He was considered a pioneer of 'television terrorism,' using high-profile attacks against Israelis for media impact. Arafat shared the 1994 Nobel Peace Prize with Israeli leaders Yitzhak Rabin and Shimon Peres for their work on the 1993 Oslo Accords. The Oslo agreement was initially seen as a potential breakthrough for an independent Palestinian state and lasting peace with Israel. However, Arafat rejected an Israeli peace deal based on the Oslo framework in 2000, leading to a Palestinian uprising that lasted over four years. Israel, in response to increased terror attacks, severely restricted Arafat's movement, confining him to his Ramallah compound in the West Bank in December 2001. Sandrine Amiel reported from Paris, and Chelsea J. Carter wrote and reported from Atlanta.
translated_content: Paris (CNN) -- Witarsa Yasser Arafat ta yi tambaya a ranar Talata game da sakamakon binciken masana kimiyya na Faransa da ke cewa shugaban Falasdinawa ya mutu ne sakamakon abubuwa na dabi'a, wanda ya saba wa zargin guba ta hanyar sinadarin polonium mai dauke da rediyo. Sakamakon binciken na Faransa, wanda kafafen yada labarai da dama ciki har da Reuters suka ruwaito, ya saba wa ra'ayin masana kimiyya na kasar Switzerland wadanda suka nuna a watan da ya gabata cewa samfuran da aka dauka daga gawar Arafat sun yi daidai da yiwuwar kamuwa da sinadarin polonium-210, duk da cewa ba su tabbatar da guba ba. 'Na gamsu da cewa akwai wani abu da ba daidai ba, kuma bai mutu ta hanyar dabi'a ba,' in ji Suha Arafat a wani taron manema labarai a birnin Paris. Tana neman a raba sakamakon binciken na Switzerland da hukumomin Faransa da ke gudanar da bincike kan mutuwar mijinta. Ta lura da bambancin kwarewar masana a Switzerland da Faransa. 'Ba na shakkar gwanintarsu, amma suna da kwarewa da kuma fannonin likita daban-daban,' in ji ta. Sakamakon binciken na Faransa ba zai kawar da jita-jitar da ake yadawa cewa an yi wa Arafat guba ba. Arafat ya mutu yana da shekaru 75 a wani asibitin soji a birnin Paris a watan Nuwamba na 2004 bayan zubar jini a kwakwalwa da kuma shiga suma. Kafin rasuwarsa, jami'an Falasdinu sun bayar da rahoton cewa Arafat yana fama da matsalar jini, ban da cutar sankarau, da kuma matsalolin narkewar abinci. Jita-jitar guba ta karade a lokacin amma jami'an Falasdinu sun karyata. Makwanni biyu bayan mutuwar Arafat, dan yayansa ya lura cewa bayanan likita ba su bayyana musabbabin mutuwar ba. Nasser al-Kidwa, wanda a lokacin shi ne wakilin Falasdinu a Majalisar Dinkin Duniya, ya ce gwaje-gwajen guba sun nuna 'babu wata guba da aka gano,' amma bai kawar da yiwuwar guba a matsayin dalilin mutuwar ba. Polonium-210 ta shahara a cikin 2006 lokacin da aka yi amfani da ita wajen kashe Alexander Litvinenko, tsohon jami'in KGB wanda ya sauya sheka zuwa Birtaniya a 2000 bayan ya tonawa FSB asiri, wanda ya gaji KGB. A cikin wasiyyarsa ta karshe daga wani asibiti a Landan, Litvinenko ya zargi shugaban Rasha Vladimir Putin, zargin da fadar Kremlin ta musanta. Falastinawa, wadanda ke kallon Arafat a matsayin alamar juriya, guba ta shafi zuciyarsu sosai. Arafat da farko ya jagoranci kungiyar 'Yantar da Palasdinu, wadda ta kai hare-hare kan wuraren Isra'ila. Daga baya ya jagoranci Hukumar Palasdinu bayan an mayar da wasu sassan Yammacin Kogin Jodan da Gaza ga ikon Palasdinu. An dauke shi a matsayin majagaba na 'ta'addancin talabijin,' yana amfani da hare-hare kan Isra'ilawa don samun tallafi a kafafen yada labarai. Arafat ya raba lambar yabo ta Nobel ta shekarar 1994 tare da shugabannin Isra'ila Yitzhak Rabin da Shimon Peres saboda aikin da suka yi a kan yarjejeniyar Oslo ta 1993. An fara ganin yarjejeniyar Oslo a matsayin wata dama ta samar da kasar Palasdinu mai cin gashin kanta da kuma dawwamammen zaman lafiya da Isra'ila. Sai dai, Arafat ya ki amincewa da yarjejeniyar zaman lafiya da Isra'ila bisa tsarin Oslo a shekarar 2000, wanda ya haifar da tashin hankalin Palasdinu da ya dauki sama da shekaru hudu. Isra'ila, a matsayin martani ga karuwar hare-haren ta'addanci, ta takaita zirga-zirgar Arafat, inda ta tsare shi a harabar Ramallah da ke Yammacin Kogin Jodan a watan Disamba na 2001. Sandrine Amiel ta ruwaito daga birnin Paris, kuma Chelsea J. Carter ta rubuta kuma ta ruwaito daga Atlanta.

article_content: A search party in Arizona's Grand Canyon National Park discovered a body on Saturday, which they believe to be that of Bryce Gillies, a 20-year-old hiker who had been reported missing, according to the National Park Service. Gillies, a student at Northern Arizona University, embarked on a backpacking excursion last Saturday, intending to return by Monday. He was planning to hike through the Deer Creek-Thunder River region of the park. After Gillies was reported missing, a search operation commenced on Tuesday. Approximately 50 volunteers and staff members from the Grand Canyon and nearby parks participated in the search. On Saturday, at approximately 9:30 a.m. (7:30 a.m. ET), one of the search teams located a body in the Bonita Creek area. The NPS stated that the body 'has been presumptively identified' as Gillies. The NPS further explained that 'The body will be recovered by helicopter using a long-line operation and taken to the Coconino County Medical Examiner.' This marks the second fatality at Grand Canyon National Park this month. The park is a globally recognized destination that welcomes around 5 million visitors each year. Earlier in July, a man from California intentionally drove his car off the edge of the canyon's South Rim, falling about 600 feet into the ravine. His death, which occurred on July 13, was determined to be a suicide. According to Michael Ghiglieri and Thomas Myers, the authors of 'Over the Edge: Death in Grand Canyon,' over 100 hikers perished at the park between 1925 and 2006, with fatal falls accounting for half of those incidents.

article_content: By Leon Watson UPDATED: 07:42 EST, February 28, 2013 The four daughters of NYPD detective Peter Figoski, who was shot dead in a botched robbery, will today share memories of the father Lamont Pride stole from them. NYPD detective Peter Figoski was fatally shot by Lamont Pride in the East New York neighborhood of Brooklyn in December 2011. Today, his daughters will confront Pride in court during his sentencing. Pride was convicted of second-degree murder, manslaughter, and burglary in Brooklyn Supreme Court earlier this month but was acquitted of aggravated murder. He faces up to 45 years in prison. Family man: Police officer Peter Figoski, who had more than 22 years of experience before being shot in the line of duty, is pictured with his four daughters. Killer: Lamont Pride, pictured at his indictment in 2011, fatally shot NYPD officer Peter Figoski in a botched robbery in East New York. Eldest daughter Christine Figoski, 21, told the New York Post: 'We talked about the things he's going to miss – our graduations, our proms, our weddings, and his grandchildren.' 'In the statement, we mention his dreams, things that he wanted to do but never got to do. He always wanted to go to the Grand Canyon, he wanted to get a motorcycle,' she said. 'He wanted to buy more land so he could build on it.' During the trial, Caitlyn Figoski had to leave the courtroom at one point as the jury heard in gruesome detail how Pride allegedly shot him in the face at close range. The New York Daily News reported that the young woman nearly fainted and needed assistance from her mother, Paulette, to exit; the distressed woman did not return until opening statements were nearly over. New York City police officer Peter Figoski's father, Frank Figoski, and daughter Corrine arrive for the first day of the murder trial of the men accused of shooting him. New York City police officer Peter Figoski's ex-wife, Paulette Figoski, was also at the proceedings. During his 22-year career in the force, Figoski earned 12 medals and made more than 200 arrests. He was posthumously promoted to detective first-class. Figoski's top priority was always his daughters, and it was widely known he delayed retirement to ensure he had enough money to put them all through college. His funeral drew approximately 20,000 police officers, family members, and friends to the church in Long Island where the girls and their father were all baptized. Show of strength: Approximately 20,000 police officers, family members, and friends came to pay their last respects to Figoski at his funeral. Support: Christine remembered that it was so busy, officers had lined up along the railroad tracks to pay their respects. He was accused of trying to steal from a marijuana dealer in a basement apartment in the Brooklyn neighborhood of East New York. When the gang allegedly broke in and began beating the dealer, a neighbor called 911. Figoski and his partner were providing backup to two officers when Pride and another man tried to flee, police said. During a struggle between his partner and one of the suspects, Figoski came face-to-face with Pride, who allegedly shot him before the officer could draw his own weapon. He died in the hospital hours later.

A lokacin da ya shafe shekaru 22 yana aiki a rundunar, Figoski ya samu lambobin yabo 12 kuma ya kama mutane fiye da 200. An ƙara masa girma zuwa ɗan sanda na farko bayan rasuwarsa. Babban abin da ya fi damun Figoski shi ne ’ya’yansa mata, kuma an san cewa ya jinkirta yin ritaya don ya tabbatar yana da isassun kuɗin da zai biya musu kuɗin jami’a. Jana’izarsa ta jawo kimanin ’yan sanda 20,000, ’yan uwa, da abokai zuwa cocin da ke Long Island inda aka yi wa ’ya’yan matan da mahaifinsu baftisma. Nunin ƙarfi: Kimanin ’yan sanda 20,000, ’yan uwa, da abokai sun zo don girmama Figoski a jana’izarsa. Goyon baya: Christine ta tuna cewa wurin ya yi cunkus sosai, har ’yan sanda sun yi layi a gefen titin jirgin ƙasa don girmamawa. An tuhume shi da ƙoƙarin yin sata daga hannun wani mai sayar da wiwi a wani ɗaki a ƙasa a unguwar East New York da ke Brooklyn. Lokacin da gungun ’yan fashin suka shiga suka fara dukan mai sayarwar, wani maƙwabci ya kira 911. Figoski da abokin aikinsa suna ba da tallafi ga wasu ƴan sanda biyu lokacin da Pride da wani mutum suka yi ƙoƙarin tserewa, kamar yadda ƴan sanda suka bayyana. A lokacin da abokin aikinsa da ɗaya daga cikin waɗanda ake zargin ke kokawa, Figoski ya fuskanci Pride, wanda ake zargin ya harbe shi kafin jami’in ya iya zaro makaminsa. Ya rasu a asibiti sa’o’i kaɗan bayan haka.

article_content: A homeless man who found a backpack containing tens of thousands of dollars in cash and traveler's checks returned it to police in Boston, stating that even if he were desperate, he wouldn't have kept ‘even a penny.’ Glen James, the Good Samaritan, was honored by Boston Police Commissioner Edward Davis on Monday. He received a special citation and was thanked for an ‘extraordinary show of character and honesty.’ James stated in a handwritten statement at a news conference that he was glad to ensure the bag and its contents were returned to the owner. Glen James said that even if he were desperate, he wouldn't have kept 'even a penny' of the tens of thousands of dollars in cash and traveler's checks he found on Saturday. ‘Even if I were desperate for money, I would not have kept even a penny,’ he said. James, who said he once worked as a Boston courthouse employee, found the backpack at the South Bay Mall in the city's Dorchester neighborhood on Saturday evening. He flagged down a police officer and handed it over. The backpack contained $2,400 in U.S. currency, almost $40,000 in traveler's checks, Chinese passports, and other personal papers. The man who lost the backpack informed workers at a nearby Best Buy store in the mall, who then called police. The backpack found by James contained $2,400 in cash and $39,500 in American Express Travelers Cheques, along with Chinese passports and other personal papers. Officers brought the backpack's owner to a nearby police station and returned his property after confirming his ownership. Authorities stated that the backpack's owner preferred to remain anonymous but was a Chinese student visiting another student in Boston. James, who did not disclose his age, said he is from the Boston area and has been homeless since 2005. A police spokeswoman stated that authorities also do not know his age but that James is staying at a city homeless shelter, and many people have expressed interest in helping him since hearing about his good deed. James said in his statement that he worked as a file clerk in the Boston municipal court system for 13 years but lost his job and became homeless due to issues with his boss. James mentioned that it would be difficult for him to hold down a job because he suffers from Meniere's disease, which the Mayo Clinic describes as an inner ear disorder that causes episodes of vertigo. Glen James was honored by Boston Police Commissioner Edward Davis on Monday and thanked for an 'extraordinary show of character and honesty.' James stated that he doesn't want to be a burden to his relatives and that people at the shelter help him. He believes God has always looked after him. James receives food stamps and panhandles to earn money for laundry, transportation, and other ‘odds and ends,’ he said. On Monday, he also thanked the strangers who have given him spare change on the street. ‘It's just nice to have some money in one's pocket so that as a homeless man I don't feel absolutely broke all the time,’ he said. A fundraising page has been started on GoFundMe.com to raise money to thank James for his honesty. Ethan Whittington, who started the page, told Boston Magazine that after reading about James's actions, he wanted to contribute. He hopes to raise $50,000. ‘I thought what he did was very honorable,’ he said. An employee from the Dorchester Best Buy contacted police and reported that a customer had reported a missing backpack containing a 'large sum of money.'

Ya tsayar da wani ɗan sanda ya miƙa masa. Jakar bayan ta ƙunshi $2,400 a tsabar kuɗin Amurka, kusan $40,000 a takardun tafiya, fasfo ɗin ƙasar Sin, da sauran takardu na sirri. Mutumin da ya rasa jakar bayan ya sanar da ma'aikata a wani kantin Best Buy da ke kusa a cikin cibiyar, waɗanda suka kira 'yan sanda. Jakar bayan da James ya samu ta ƙunshi $2,400 a tsabar kuɗi da $39,500 a takardun American Express Travelers Cheques, tare da fasfo ɗin ƙasar Sin da sauran takardu na sirri. 'Yan sanda sun kai mai jakar bayan zuwa ofishin 'yan sanda da ke kusa kuma suka mayar masa da kayansa bayan sun tabbatar da mallakarsa. Mahukunta sun bayyana cewa mai jakar bayan ya fi son a ɓoye sunansa amma dalibi ne ɗan ƙasar Sin da ke ziyartar wani ɗalibi a Boston. James, wanda bai bayyana shekarunsa ba, ya ce shi ɗan yankin Boston ne kuma ya zama marar gida tun 2005. Wata mai magana da yawun 'yan sanda ta bayyana cewa mahukunta suma ba su san shekarunsa ba amma James yana zaune ne a wani matsugunin marasa gida na birni, kuma mutane da yawa sun nuna sha'awar taimaka masa tun bayan jin labarin kyakkyawan aikinsa. James ya ce a cikin sanarwarsa cewa ya yi aiki a matsayin ma'aikacin fayil a tsarin kotun birnin Boston na tsawon shekaru 13 amma ya rasa aikinsa kuma ya zama marar gida saboda matsaloli da shugabansa. James ya ambata cewa zai yi masa wuya ya riƙe aiki saboda yana fama da cutar Meniere, wanda Mayo Clinic ta bayyana a matsayin cutar kunne ta ciki wacce ke haifar da rashin daidaituwa. Kwamishinan 'yan sanda na Boston Edward Davis ya karrama Glen James a ranar Litinin kuma ya gode masa saboda 'nuna halayya da gaskiya ta musamman.' James ya bayyana cewa ba ya son ya zama nauyi ga danginsa kuma mutanen da ke matsugunin suna taimaka masa. Ya yi imani da cewa Allah ya kula da shi koyaushe. James yana karɓar tallafin abinci kuma yana bara don samun kuɗin wanki, sufuri, da sauran ‘ƙananan abubuwa,’ in ji shi. A ranar Litinin, ya kuma gode wa baƙi da suka ba shi canji a kan titi. ‘Yana da daɗi kawai a sami wasu kuɗi a cikin aljihu don ni a matsayina na marar gida ba na jin kamar ba ni da komai a kowane lokaci,’ in ji shi. An fara wani shafi na tara kuɗaɗe a GoFundMe.com don tara kuɗi don gode wa James saboda gaskiyarsa. Ethan Whittington, wanda ya fara shafin, ya gaya wa Boston Magazine cewa bayan karanta game da ayyukan James, yana son bayar da gudummawa. Yana fatan tara $50,000. ‘Na yi tunanin abin da ya yi abin girmamawa ne,’ in ji shi. Wani ma'aikaci daga Dorchester Best Buy ya tuntubi 'yan sanda kuma ya ba da rahoton cewa wani abokin ciniki ya ba da rahoton ɓacewar jakar baya ɗauke da 'babban adadin kuɗi.'

article_content: In Tacloban, Philippines, residents sift through debris in the dark, navigating murky puddles after frequent, heavy rains. Along some streets, groups huddle around small fires, cooking food amidst the wreckage. This is life in Tacloban – or, more accurately, a struggle to hold onto it. The situation has drastically changed over the past six days in this Philippine city, located approximately 575 kilometers (360 miles) southeast of Manila, on the Pacific Ocean. Super Typhoon Haiyan struck early last Friday, with sustained winds of 315 kph (195 mph) and gusts reaching 380 kph (235 mph). The impact of Haiyan is visible everywhere: most buildings are damaged or destroyed. Decomposed animal carcasses lie on the ground, alongside body bags containing human remains. While the intensity caught some off guard, most residents were aware of the impending danger. May May Gula, 30, was among those who heeded official warnings and sought shelter at the Tacloban Convention Center. She and others reached the building's upper levels when the devastating storm surge swept in from the sea, a move that likely saved their lives. Many who remained on the ground floor were killed or injured, according to Gula and her friend Lina Reforzado. By Thursday, Gula and her relatives were sharing a room on the building's ground floor with seven other families. Their homes destroyed, they, along with others, have transformed the building into a makeshift living space. Clothes hang from the upper floors, and temporary shelters built from storm debris have sprung up around the building. They finally tasted rice – a staple food in the Philippines – on Thursday, the first time in a week, after it was distributed at the convention center following the typhoon. However, they are unsure when the next delivery will arrive, and what their next steps will be. Gula stated, 'We really don't know what we're going to do next.' There are glimpses of 'normal' life around Tacloban: a pig shrieking as it is taken into a building for slaughter; an animal carcass being butchered in public; a few vendors selling pork. However, for most, food remains desperately scarce. At the airport, large groups of people are hoping to leave the devastated city. A queue of people, sheltering from the intense sun and intermittent rain under umbrellas, extends from the remains of the terminal building into the debris-filled parking area. Some appear to need urgent evacuation. One man is holding an intravenous drip for his wife, who sits on a chair, clutching a pale child. No one knows if they will be able to leave in time. CNN's Greg Botelho contributed to this report.
translated_content: A cikin Tacloban, Philippines, mazauna suna tace tarkace cikin duhu, suna ratsa kududdufai masu duhu bayan yawan ruwan sama. A wasu tituna, gungun mutane suna manne kusa da kananan wuta, suna dafa abinci a cikin rugujewar. Wannan shi ne rayuwa a Tacloban – ko kuma, mafi daidaituwa, gwagwarmaya don rike ta. Yanayin ya canza sosai a cikin kwanaki shida da suka gabata a cikin wannan birni na Philippines, wanda yake kimanin kilomita 575 (mil 360) kudu maso gabashin Manila, a kan Tekun Pasifik. Guguwar Typhoon Haiyan ta afku a farkon Juma'a da ta gabata, tare da ci gaba da iskar kilomita 315 (mil 195) da karfin iska ya kai kilomita 380 (mil 235). Tasirin Haiyan yana bayyane ko'ina: yawancin gine-gine sun lalace ko sun rushe. Gawarwakin dabbobi da suka lalace suna kwance a kasa, kusa da jakunkuna dauke da gawarwakin mutane. Yayin da tsananin ya kama wasu ba su yi tsammani ba, yawancin mazauna sun san hatsarin na zuwa. May May Gula, mai shekaru 30, na daga cikin wadanda suka bi gargadin jami'ai kuma suka nemi mafaka a Cibiyar Taro ta Tacloban. Ita da wasu sun kai matakan sama na ginin lokacin da mummunar guguwar ta mamaye daga teku, matakin da mai yiwuwa ya ceci rayuwarsu. Mutane da yawa da suka rage a bene na kasa sun mutu ko sun ji rauni, a cewar Gula da abokiyarta Lina Reforzado. Zuwa Alhamis, Gula da danginta suna raba daki a bene na kasa na ginin tare da wasu iyalai bakwai. Gidajensu sun lalace, su, tare da wasu, sun mayar da ginin zuwa wani wurin zama na wucin gadi. Tufafi suna rataye daga benaye na sama, kuma matsugunan wucin gadi da aka gina daga tarkacen guguwa sun tsiro a kusa da ginin. Daga karshe sun dandana shinkafa – babban abinci a Philippines – a ranar Alhamis, a karon farko a cikin mako guda, bayan an raba a cibiyar taro bayan guguwar. Koyaya, ba su da tabbacin lokacin da za a sake kawo kayan, da kuma matakan da za su dauka a gaba. Gula ya ce, 'Ba mu san abin da za mu yi ba a gaba.' Akwai wasu alamun 'rayuwa ta yau da kullun' a kusa da Tacloban: alade yana kururuwa yayin da ake kai shi cikin gini don a yanka shi; ana yanka gawar dabba a bainar jama'a; wasu 'yan kasuwa suna sayar da naman alade. Koyaya, ga yawancin, abinci ya kasance mai matukar karanci. A filin jirgin sama, manyan gungun mutane suna fatan barin birnin da ya lalace. Layin mutane, suna neman mafaka daga tsananin rana da ruwan sama a karkashin laima, ya tashi daga ragowar ginin tashar zuwa filin ajiye motoci da ke cike da tarkace. Wasu suna ganin kamar suna bukatar a kwashe su cikin gaggawa. Wani mutum yana rike da ruwan jiki ga matarsa, wacce ke zaune a kan kujera, tana rike da wani yaro mara lafiya. Babu wanda ya san ko za su iya fita kafin lokaci ya kure. Greg Botelho na CNN ya ba da gudummawa ga wannan rahoton.
